Ibi bigaragazwa n’ubushakashatsi bwa Citizen Report Card (CRC) bwakozwe mu 2026, bugamije kumenya uko abaturage babona imitangire ya serivisi n’imiyoborere mu nzego zibegereye.

Dr. Doris Uwicyeza Picard, Umuyobozi Mukuru w’Urwego rw’Igihugu rw’Imiyoborere (RGB), yabigarutseho kuri uyu wa Gatatu tariki ya 11 Ugushyingo 2026, ubwo yagezaga ku Nteko Ishinga Amategeko imitwe yombi raporo y’ibikorwa bya RGB by’umwaka wa 2025/2026 n’igenamigambi ry’ibikorwa by’umwaka wa 2026/2027.

Yavuze ko igabanuka ry’iki gipimo rikwiye gutuma inzego z’ibanze n’izindi zitanga serivisi zongera imbaraga mu kunoza imitangire ya serivisi no kurushaho kugira umuturage ku isonga.

Ati “Serivisi zihabwa abaturage ndetse no kugira uruhare mu bibakorerwa byagabanutseho amanota 2.9. Birakwiye ko abayobozi b’inzego z’ibanze ndetse n’izindi nzego zishinzwe guha serivisi umuturage bashyiramo imbaraga kugira ngo igipimo cy’ibyo babakorera kizamuke.”

Depite Mukabunani Christine yabajije RGB impamvu imitangire ya serivisi mu nzego zegerejwe abaturage itarateye imbere, ahubwo igipimo cy’uko abaturage bayishimira kikaba cyaragabanutse.

Dr. Uwicyeza yasobanuye ko CRC atari ubushakashatsi bugamije gusa kugaragaza amanota inzego zabonye, ahubwo ko ari igikoresho gifasha inzego kumenya aho zitanga serivisi neza n’aho hakiri ibibazo bikwiye gukemurwa.

Ati “Bigaragaza ko hakiri imbogamizi mu mitangire ya serivisi no mu miyoborere y’inzego zegereye abaturage, bityo hakaba hakenewe gukomeza kunoza imikorere yazo.”

Yavuze ko ubushakashatsi buha abaturage urubuga rwo kugaragaza uko babona imikorere y’inzego zibegereye, ibyo bishimira n’ibyo bifuza ko byahinduka.

Dr. Uwicyeza yavuze ko zimwe mu mpamvu zituma abaturage batishimira serivisi bahabwa ari uko ibibazo byabo bidakemurwa ku gihe, gusiragizwa mu gihe bashaka serivisi, ndetse no kutamenya neza urwego bagomba kwitabaza kugira ngo bahabwe serivisi runaka.

Ati “Hari aho usanga abaturage batakemurirwa ibibazo ku gihe, ahandi bakasiragizwa, ndetse hari n’abaturage batamenya aho basabira serivisi bakeneye.”

MN202611_5cbrzd4og7.t:
President Prabowo (left) said he was sorry to lose Gibran Rakabuming Raka (right), who has been mired in a growing controversy over his high school credentials

Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka tendered his resignation to parliament on Thursday, triggering the process of finding his replacement amid growing turmoil for the government.

Gibran had been facing impeachment calls after a Supreme Court ruling that a high-school document used during his 2024 election campaign was invalid.

His departure comes amid a faltering political alliance between his father, ex-president Joko Widodo, and the incumbent President Prabowo Subianto.

Standing alongside Gibran, Prabowo told reporters he had accepted his resignation with "a heavy heart". Upper house lawmakers will have 60 days to fill the vacancy from two candidates nominated by the president.

"[Gibran] has demonstrated a chivalrous attitude, a strong sense of responsibility, and the qualities of a statesman," Prabowo said, adding that the resignation was "for the benefit of the nation, the state, and the people of Indonesia".

"He certainly believes that he completed his education through a proper and structured process. However, we must understand that educational systems abroad differ from those in Indonesia," the president said.

Gibran has long faced controversy over whether his high school qualifications met legal requirements to run for office.

Having studied in Singapore and Australia, he had used an Indonesian equivalence certificate to demonstrate his educational credentials.

Indonesian law requires vice-presidents to have completed senior secondary school or its equivalent, but the Supreme Court found no evidence to prove Gibran had graduated.

"No evidence was found to show Gibran had a foreign diploma or certificate that could serve as the basis for equivalency with a senior high school or equivalent qualification," it said.

It also considered a Constitutional Court ruling from earlier in October which came to the same conclusion.

The Supreme Court ruling prompted more than 100 lawmakers to support a parliamentary initiative that could have paved the way for proceedings to impeach Gibran.

Gibran previously argued that undertaking university education was sufficient proof that he had completed senior high school.

On Tuesday, he asked for the chance to challenge the ruling and be given the opportunity to prove the legitimacy of his education credentials, State Secretariat Prasetyo Hadi said.

Gibran's ascension to Prabowo's ticket in the 2024 election was part of an alliance formed between his father, outgoing president Joko Widodo - known as Jokowi - and Prabowo, his erstwhile bitter rival.

Gibran was 36 at the time, and only became eligible for candidacy after a controversial ruling by the Constitutional Court, which exempted him from the minimum age requirement of 40.

But tensions between Jokowi and Prabowo appear to have flared.

Since taking the presidency, Prabowo has shown little interest in pushing ahead with Jokowi's legacy project: the construction of Nusantara, a new capital. Instead, he has focused much of the state's resources on his own flagship programme to provide free school meals across the country.

In a series of personnel reshuffles over the past year, Prabowo has also shifted many Jokowi loyalists into new roles, including long-serving finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati.

Last week, authorities arrested several senior officials, including presidential chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo - no relation to Prabowo - on suspicions of wiretapping the president.

Prabowo sacked Listyo a day later, in what many pointed to as a sign of a crumbling alliance: Listyo, who formerly served as the national police chief, is widely considered a long-time ally of Jokowi.

Within the government, allegiances seem to be shifting. On Monday, three members of Prabowo's cabinet collectively resigned from the party led by Kaesang Pangarep, Jokowi's youngest son, citing their desire to focus on their duties in Prabowo's administration.

But neither man has confirmed the rift. Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Jokowi said he still supported Prabowo's leadership.

Jokowi also said Gibran's resignation was part of "political dynamics" and he had told his son "the position was temporary".

All this is unfolding at a particularly turbulent period in Prabowo's presidency. The free school meals programme is struggling for funding, parts of Indonesia have recently battled the country's worst wildfires in a decade, and the national stock market faces crisis amid allegations of widespread market manipulation.

Across the country, students and activists have staged demonstrations to protest against the government's handling of a range of issues, including the environmental crisis and corruption.

Brian Curson has been involved in football for more than 40 years

A Pro Ref referee observer has been suspended for nine weeks and fined £200 for making discriminatory remarks after a match he was working at.

Brian Curson had visited Kenilworth Road to assess the officials at the League One fixture between Luton Town and Rotherham United on 15 November 2025.

An allegation was made that Curson made two discriminatory comments in the lounge at Luton's stadium after the game, which led to the Football Association investigation.

Curson was charged with acting in an improper manner and/or using abusive and/or insulting words.

It was considered an 'aggravated breach', using words which included a reference - whether express or implied - to ethnic origin, race or nationality.

Curson, who no longer works for Pro Ref, said that he did not recall making the comments but the FA commission "was satisfied on the balance of probabilities" that they had been made.

The FA requested a time-based sanction because of Curson's role in the sport, as a player would serve a suspension of between nine and 12 matches.

It was determined that, taking into account Curson's experience and role on the day of the match, he should be suspended for nine weeks.

Curson was also told he must attend a mandatory education programme, and received a warning as to future conduct.

Michael Skubala has won five of his 15 league games in charge of Bristol City

Bristol City will give under-pressure head coach Michael Skubala the chance to improve their results, particularly at home, says chief executive Charlie Boss.

The Robins have lost their past four Championship matches at Ashton Gate, culminating in last Saturday's 5-0 drubbing by Norwich City which left them in 17th place.

"The game against Norwich was a long way short of our standards and in the days that followed there have been a lot of tough and honest conversations around the building," said Boss in a video message on the club website. , external

"Earlier this week the board met and we agreed to give Michael Skubala the opportunity to turn around the home form."

Skubala led Lincoln City to the League One title last season before joining Bristol City on a three-year-deal in May.

However, a run of only two wins from their past 10 matches has led to supporters voicing their concerns.

"A lot of fans made their feelings known loud and clear at Ashton Gate on Saturday and I want them to know everybody shares their frustration from the owners, the board and the players," added Boss.

"Michael Skubala more than anyone knows we need to improve - we wouldn't have made this decision if we didn't believe that together we can get through this difficult period."

Bristol City's next Championship match is at second-placed Middlesbrough on Saturday, 21 November (15:00 GMT) before home games against Wrexham and Swansea sandwich a trip to West Bromwich Albion.

On Thursday Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Moscow and Dublin to hold talks with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents

Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day.

Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion.

However, both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon.

Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest."

"I believe the Russians came with very strict directives, so it was extremely difficult to soften the discussion," he said. But he added that he felt "good momentum" and urged for a second round of talks to be organised as soon as possible.

Comments by Kremlin negotiator Vladimir Medinsky were less conciliatory. "Right now... a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the US, and on whether Europe comes to its senses," he said.

After the talks it was announced that on Thursday US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner - President Donald Trump's son-in-law - would travel to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to speak to Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky.

The meetings in Abu Dhabi had been framed as centred around the "security architecture" of Europe.

For Kyiv, this may include reassurances that allies will come to its aid if Ukraine comes under attack again, despite the country not being a Nato member.

For Moscow, a reworked "security framework" is likely to include a limit to the influence of Nato in eastern Europe - a central concern for the Kremlin since the alliance's eastward expansion.

Earlier this week Kushner said the US hoped to "create a new framework" of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that could "secure lasting peace", while the Kremlin's Medinsky said the world needed a "new" and "fair" security system.

That framework would serve as "a new Yalta and Potsdam", Medinsky said, referring to the 1940s summits in which the victorious Allied powers carved up post-war Europe into spheres of influence.

Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin.

Representatives of Britain, Nato and various EU countries were also in Abu Dhabi and met with US and Ukrainian negotiators, but the Kremlin - with whom the EU does not officially communicate - said its delegation had not had any contact with them.

Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent.

Many - particularly in eastern Europe - feel their security is linked to that of Ukraine. Agreements cannot be implemented "if no consensus can be reached among Nato members," a German government spokesperson said on Wednesday.

Kushner said the US was keen to bring the Europeans on board and said that getting them "added to the format" would be on the agenda for his talks with Putin.

There is also disagreement on whether discussions on a future security framework should be preceded by a ceasefire, as the Europeans and Kyiv would want, or whether the fighting only stops after an agreement has been reached, as the Kremlin has insisted.

Any agreement on a peacetime security framework, however, is contingent on the war ending, Kushner noted. But that cannot occur "until there's an agreement on territory and on all other bilateral issues," he added.

Since talks began last year, a core obstacle to any settlement has been Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are essential to its security.

Moscow, meanwhile, has never backed down from its demand that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds. "Every inch" of land would be "returned to Russia one way or another", Medinsky said.

Kushner acknowledged that the territorial question remained the hardest, while Zelensky's chief of staff and negotiator Kyrylo Budanov refused to be drawn on whether Russia was still demanding a Ukrainian withdrawal from the region.

Later, Budanov admitted the talks had been "tough" and that Ukraine's priority was to ensure Russia could not attack it again.

"These deals are very hard and complex, and this one is very emotional, very complex," Kushner said. "The reality is there is no trust right now between the sides and that is to be expected after a conflict like this."

Leonardo Bertulazzi was first arrested in Buenos Aires in 2002

A 74-year-old Italian man who was found guilty of a kidnapping carried out by a far-left militant group in the 1970s has escaped while under house arrest in Argentina and is on the run.

Leonardo Bertulazzi used a harness to abseil down from a fifth-floor balcony in the capital, Buenos Aires.

His escape was not immediately registered because he had tampered with his electronic ankle monitor so that it continued to transmit body temperature measurements even after he had prised it open and absconded.

Bertulazzi already spent decades as a fugitive after he was sentenced in absentia in Italy for the 1977 kidnapping of Italian naval engineer Pietro Costa.

He was awaiting extradition to Italy and was being monitored by the Argentine ministry of security through an ankle tag which registers the wearer's body temperature and movements.

Officials said that they had become suspicious when they noticed that the tag had remained stationary.

When they entered the fifth-floor apartment in the centre of Buenos Aires, Bertulazzi was gone, but the ankle monitor remained.

Wary of Bertulazzi's past with the Marxist guerilla group the Red Brigades and his bomb-making skills, police called in explosives experts in case it had been rigged to detonate, according to Argentine newspaper Clarín.

However, the experts found that while Bertulazzi had tampered with the device, he had done so to prevent the alarm from sounding once he removed it.

Italian media say that his extradition to Italy had been imminent after his last appeal was rejected.

Bertulazzi was first arrested after using a false passport to cross into Argentina from neighbouring Chile in 2002.

However, he was granted refugee status in 2004 and lived freely in the South American country until his re-arrest in 2024, when the current right-wing president, Javier Milei, took office.

Milei's government said at the time that "Bertulazzi is responsible for crimes that undermined democratic values and the lives of many victims".

He was a member of the Red Brigades, which kidnapped and killed a number of state officials in the 1970s and '80s.

Bertulazzi was part of the Red Brigades' Genoa section that kidnapped Pietro Costa on the street and then held him for 81 days before receiving a big ransom.

The money it made from the kidnapping was then used to buy a flat in Rome, which was used in 1978 for the Red Brigades' most notorious crime, the kidnap and murder of Italian former Prime Minister, Aldo Moro.

Moro was abducted when his car was ambushed on the way to the opening of parliament. He was held in the flat for 54 days before he was shot and his body abandoned in the boot of a Renault car in the centre of Rome.

Cholera cases are being reported in several parts of Bujumbura, Burundi’s commercial capital, as residents face shortages of clean water and limited access to sanitation.

SOS Médias Burundi reports that patients from Gihosha and nearby areas have been taken to King Khaled and Prince Louis Rwagasore hospitals. Health authorities are concerned about the disease spreading among communities with inadequate hygiene and sanitation.

A patient receiving treatment at King Khaled Hospital for another illness said new cholera patients had continued to arrive since the previous week.

“Things are worrying. Since last week, they have continued receiving patients. Not a day passes without a new case being reported,” the patient told SOS Médias Burundi.

The patient also raised concerns about delays in medical assessment and the time it takes to separate suspected cholera patients from others at the hospital.

Those being treated for other conditions fear they could become infected, the patient said, urging health workers to assess and treat suspected cases promptly.

Residents in parts of Gihosha, northern Bujumbura and surrounding areas say they struggle to find safe drinking water.

The shortages have heightened fears that the disease could spread further.

Cholera is an intestinal infection that can spread through water or food contaminated with the bacteria that cause it. It can lead to severe watery diarrhoea and vomiting, causing dangerous fluid loss. Without prompt treatment, it can be fatal.

Cases have also been reported elsewhere in Burundi. In Kizuka and Gatete, in Rumonge District, Burunga Province, SOS Médias Burundi reported cases during one week in late October.

Its figures cite 10 cases, seven patients still in hospital, one person who died at home and three who had recovered.

Those outcomes add up to 11, so the reported total requires clarification.

The outbreak is raising concern in areas where access to clean water remains limited. Poor sanitation, open defecation and contamination of water sources can help spread the infection.

The film has been funded by BBC Film, BFI, Sky, Screen Yorkshire and CML Entertainment Finance

Bafta-winning actors Toby Jones and Emily Watson have finished work on a film about the scientist behind Britain's first spacecraft to land on Mars, which got "lost".

Mars Express, directed by Mackenzie Crook, will see Jones play Colin Pillinger while Watson is his wife Judith.

The couple began developing the unmanned Beagle 2 probe to search for life on Mars while Pillinger was a professor of planetary sciences at the Open University in Milton Keynes. The probe went out of contact upon landing in December 2003, until it was finally spotted in 2015, after Pillinger died.

Crook said: "It's a complete honour to be telling the extraordinary story... for my first feature film as director."

Pillinger died believing that Beagle 2 had not safely landed on Mars

Pillinger, originally from Kingswood near Bristol, became a familiar face in the 1990s as he sought public support and funding for the ambitious mission, enlisting celebrities and pop stars to help promote it.

Beagle 2 was launched into space on board the European Space Agency's Mars Express orbiter.

His Beagle 2 lander was due to touch down on 25 December 2003, but failed to send a signal confirming it had landed safely.

The mission was considered a failure for years, however, in January 2015 images taken by US space agency Nasa showed the lander had reached the surface safely.

Pillinger died eight months earlier following a brain haemorrhage.

Mars Express is the first feature-length film to be directed by actor Mackenzie Crook

The director added: "Joe Bone's beautiful script has made it easy to attract some of the best names in the business to join our brilliantly creative team and I'm thrilled to be working once again with my friend Toby Jones."

Crook, known for his roles in The Office and Pirates of the Caribbean, previously worked with Jones on Detectorists , the BBC's Bafta-winning comedy he wrote, directed and starred in.

He also starred in Small Prophets, a comedy which made its debut on BBC Two and the BBC iPlayer in February.

The film is expected to be released in 2027.

MN202611_5elh6fedn9.t:
Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page is to take part in the 26th series of I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here

Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page has confirmed she will appear on the upcoming reality TV series I'm a Celebrity, with her former co-star Ruth Jones urging her to "have a crackin' time".

Page, who played Stacey Shipman in the BBC comedy, is joining this year's line-up of celebrities on the forthcoming show in Australia.

The 49-year-old, from Swansea, said she had her sights on becoming the first Welsh Queen of the Jungle.

"You makes Barry very proud, I'm not gonna lie," said Jones - assuming her former Gavin and Stacey character Nessa Jenkins - on Instagram.

"They're gonna make you stick all manner of matter in your gob. And I'm not talking Gwen's omelettes... Just don't over do it, alrigh'? You knows what a weak constitution you has."

Joanna Page, pictured with Ruth Jones (right), has her sights on becoming the first Welsh Queen of the I'm a Celeb jungle

Speaking ahead of her trip down under, Page said she believed her co-stars will be "shocked" when she arrives in the jungle for the ITV reality show.

"I also know they will find it funny. They know exactly what I am like and they will laugh."

Page said being the first Welsh queen would be a "pretty good title to take home", but added she was just as excited to see how long she could last.

"I'm going to see this to the end and I'm going to be strong. I am going to get the most out of this."

Eleven celebrities will enter the Australian jungle camp on Monday

As a mother-of-four, Page said she hoped her part in the show will help her "reconnect" with who she was before becoming a mum.

"This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. I'm very much an impulsive person and I just make a gut decision, so I said 'yes' straight away," said Page.

She said she hoped to find "peace and time for my thoughts" away from the everyday worries about feeding the children and getting everyone ready for the school run.

"I can be me, I can be Jo and not just mummy all the time. I think that will be nice."

"I will never get to do anything like this again. I am telling myself, 'Come on Jo, let's take yourself off to Australia and give yourself an experience'.

"It's exciting and it's going to be life-changing."

Ruth Jones - aka Nessa - said she was "so excited" to see Joanna Page head to the Australian jungle

Page will enter the jungle alongside footballer Wayne Rooney, TV personality Chloe Burrows and soap star Claire Sweeney.

Rooney will follow in his wife Coleen's footsteps after she finished as runner-up on the 2024 series, and said he hoped "people will see me for who I am".

He said he had "always wanted to do" the show, joking that because of his short-lived football managerial career, he had more time on his hands.

"I like to have fun and I like to think I am actually a fun guy to be around.

"I do like to mess around a bit and I do talk a lot. People will have their own opinions, but I hope they will see me as a genuine person."

Page will be also joined by Paralympian and TV presenter Ade Adepitan - who will be the first contestant in a wheelchair to appear on the show – something he said his eight-year-old self would not believe.

"Words like 'honour' and 'privilege' are the ones I feel, but I don't think they sum it up enough," he said.

"For me, this is a moment in time. Even if I go out in the first week, I will always be remembered as the person in a wheelchair. I am slightly overwhelmed.

"It's never been done before, and it never crossed my mind I would be the first.

I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here! starts on Monday 16 November at 21:00 GMT on ITV.

Watch: Protesters and police clash in Barcelona

Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.

Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas.

Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption.

Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November.

The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant."

There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields.

Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de Gràcia, close to the iconic Plaça de Catalunya in the centre of the city.

Small fires burned in the middle of the streets as bins were set alight. Local media reported that a group of people fired fireworks towards police and looted shops including the Lego store. Protesters were also seen trying to enter the Apple Store.

The BBC spoke to a woman who attended the protests in Barcelona who said it was mostly very peaceful and "joyful". She said she was there to protest about the housing costs and that "there were a lot of children and old people there."

She was in the area of Las Ramblas in the evening and saw fires in the streets. "The fires were everywhere, it was very intense," she said.

Earlier in the day there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads.

The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices.

Police said they had made dozens of arrests

"We've completely brought the city to a standstill," a protester in Madrid told Reuters news agency, adding there was widespread support for the general strike. "Everyone's out there, despite the rainy weather; everyone's out on the streets."

Another protester, 37-year-old teacher Olga Domingo, said she was protesting because "the housing situation is outrageous. The current cost of living compared to wages is completely unsustainable".

The strike was triggered by widespread protests over affordable housing and rising living costs, after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from a flat in Madrid where she had lived for seven decades. She died in hospital weeks later.

Rental prices in the capital have risen in recent years. The monthly cost of a 50 sq m apartment in Madrid was an average of €1,170 ($1,300; £1,000) in October, according to property portal Idealista, while Spain's average gross monthly salary is about €2,460.

That amounts to nearly half the average gross salary, well above the 30% level of affordability often recommended by housing experts and public institutions.

Watch: Protesters gather across Spain for first general strike in 14 years

Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called snap elections last month after parliament failed to approve his plan for housing reform.

Not since 2012, under the conservative government of Mariano Rajoy, has Spain held general strikes.

And while previous strikes have been problematic for the government in power, this one is different. Sánchez and his ministers have even encouraged workers to down tools and demand affordable housing.

"Your eight-hour day. Your pension. Your public healthcare… These were collective conquests," he wrote on social media, praising those who took part in previous strikes.

Tyres were set on fire in the city of Gijon in northern Spain

The conservative People's Party (PP), by contrast, has accused the government of attempting to weaponise the strike for electoral gain.

PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo called the general strike "nonsense", calling the unions "mafia" and "trash". Feijoo's party is leading in the polls and party spokesman Miguel Tellado accused the government of exploiting the strike to warn voters against allowing a right-wing government to be formed, which looks the most likely outcome of the 29 November election.

Sánchez told Spanish TV this week: "What is nonsense is to question the rights of workers to strike."

Among those taking part in the general strike was Gonzalo Álvarez, 27, who was visiting different picket lines in central Madrid.

Although he works in sales, he has been volunteering for a housing union that tries to protect tenants and makes them aware of their rights.

The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal at the end of September "was the little fire" that sparked this protest, he told the BBC.

Álvarez knew the 87-year-old, who had faced a tripling of her rent under new landlords, and says he was deeply upset by her treatment.

He rents a small, one-bedroom flat with his girlfriend, a dental hygienist, in the city's southern Arganzuela disrict. The couple pay €1,000 between them, which means each spends about half of their salary on housing, even before other bills.

"It's absolutely crazy… with the food, with the electricity, with the water, with gas."

He sees no way of getting on the property ladder: "You have to collect an insane amount of money to be able to buy a house. So with these salaries, it's impossible."

With current rent and purchase prices, he believes buying somewhere is "completely impossible".

Gonzalo Álvarez, who was taking part in the general strike, says 50% of his salary goes towards rent

However, the vice-president of the CEOE, Spanish biggest business association, Miguel Garrido, criticised the strike, complaining that businesses had little to do with the price of housing.

"This is not a strike for labour-related reasons, but rather for political ones, and it is closely linked to the early calling of elections," he said.

Demonstrations were planned for some of Spain's biggest cities later in the day and the scale of support will be widely viewed as an indicator of public discontent ahead of the election.

Another reliable indicator of support for strikes is the level of demand for electricity with Spain's industrial sector.

Power usage in Spain fell by 7.5% during the early hours of Wednesday, according to data from operator Red Eléctrica. During the last general strike 14 years ago, equivalent consumption was down by more than 15%.

A household may find cheaper cooking gas nearby but be unable to buy it because its cylinder carries another company’s brand.

Clément Nzayisenga, owner of Clément Shop Gaz in Kigali’s Muhima area, says this limits consumer choice and makes it harder for small retailers to compete.

Nzayisenga is asking the Ministry of Trade and Industry, RURA and the Private Sector Federation to establish a system allowing customers to refill cylinders at different licensed suppliers, provided the cylinders meet safety standards.

He also wants regulators to examine how wholesale prices are set and ensure damaged or expired cylinders are removed from circulation.

Prices advertised by different suppliers show the variation. SP’s reported price is Rwf 11,670 for a 6kg refill and Rwf 23,340 for 12kg. Jibu Rwanda lists 6kg at Rwf 12,400 and 12kg at Rwf 25,000.

Tekeraheza lists 6kg at Rwf 12,500 online or Rwf 13,000 for walk-in service, and 12kg at Rwf 25,000 online or Rwf 26,000 walk-in.

CANA GAZ lists 6kg at Rwf 13,500 and 12kg at Rwf 26,500. MIGRO lists 6kg at Rwf 20,000 and 12kg at Rwf 35,000.

These are advertised prices and may vary by location, delivery cost, cylinder brand and service terms.

Prices can also vary by location. The New Times reported that 12kg cylinders sold for about Rwf 27,000 in Kabuga and around Rwf 28,000 in parts of Rwamagana and Huye.

Retailers cited transport and distribution costs. The report also said regulators no longer set standard cooking gas prices.

The comparisons are not perfectly alike, but they underline the dilemma Nzayisenga describes. A cheaper supplier offers little choice if a customer’s cylinder cannot be refilled there.

Any cylinder exchange system would need strict inspection and tracking to protect safety.

The issue is not new. In 2023, lawmakers raised concerns about gas prices, and then a joint team involving RURA and the Ministry of Finance was examining pricing. No updates on the findings or decisions have been made public so far.

Nzayisenga’s proposal renews questions about how to protect consumers from high costs while keeping the market safe and competitive.

A fire destroyed all belongings in the boys’ dormitory at Musamvu Technical and Vocational College (TCC) in Kibungo Sector, Ngoma District.

Ngoma District Executive Secretary Ingabire Benoît confirmed the incident. The dining area was spared, but nothing inside the dormitory was recovered intact. The cause of the fire has not yet been established.

The fire broke out while students were attending classes, and no students were inside the dormitory. Police responded and extinguished the blaze before it could spread to other school buildings.

Kibungo Sector officials said they were working with other authorities and partners to provide students with essential supplies so they can continue their studies. “We want to assure parents that no student was in the building when the fire broke out,” the sector executive secretary told the press.

The incident comes amid a series of major fires reported in Rwanda since October, causing losses worth billions of francs.

Police recently launched a public campaign urging people to take steps to prevent fires and use available equipment to contain them while waiting for emergency responders.

Lina Attalah has said Egypt is "trying to limit the already-limited space" for independent media

A criminal court in Cairo has postponed the retrial of the prominent Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, whose case has drawn international condemnation.

Wednesday's opening hearing was adjourned until 18 November after defence lawyers representing the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr requested a new judge.

The UN has warned of "widening assaults on press freedom by Egyptian authorities, including the targeting, persecution and harassment of independent journalists".

Attalah told the BBC that a recent crackdown was meant to "send a chilling message" to "the very few newsrooms that are left".

She warned: "Everybody should be careful, everybody should be scared, everybody should be wondering if they are next."

Set up 13 years ago, Mada Masr became Egypt's leading independent news site with Attalah as its editor-in-chief and co-founder.

Last month, the New Cairo Misdemeanours Court convicted her of running a website without a licence - which she said she had tried in vain for years to obtain. She was issued a hefty fine of 3 million Egyptian pounds ($56,000; £42,000) and Mada Masr was ordered to shut down.

After that trial, Attalah found that a court had previously given her a one-year prison sentence, without her knowledge, for "spreading false news" - a charge often used against journalists and dissidents - as well as operating a website without a licence. It was issued in absentia in 2024, even though she was in the country at the time. Attalah is now being retried in that case by the same judge.

At the opening session, Attalah's defence team requested the judge's recusal, arguing that he had "already formed a conviction in mind against the defendant", Mada Masr cited its lawyer Hassan al-Azhar as saying , external . The judge went into recess before adjourning proceedings for a week to allow the court to consider the defence's request, he added.

Mada Masr also said Attalah's appeal against last month's conviction was scheduled to take place on 25 November.

Egypt has largely stifled freedom of the press, ranking 169th out of 180 countries for press freedom, according to Reporters Without Borders' 2026 analysis. The group says that at least 26 journalists who were arrested in recent years remain in detention.

While most newspapers and television stations now keep to government lines, Mada Masr remained a rare, independent and investigative news source in Egypt. However, since 2017 the site could only be viewed from outside the country.

It had reported on alleged corruption and human rights abuses, and provided deep coverage of politics and economics, as well as regional upheaval and wars in Libya, Sudan and Gaza.

In her BBC interview on Sunday, Attalah insisted that the factual reporting and professional standards of Mada Masr had an important role to play in Egyptian society, which could benefit the government.

"It's much better if you have a little space left to have it open for professional media organisations who do rigorous reporting, because if we disappear, then you make the space for conspiracies and disinformation," she said.

"People need to know, people need to consume information and you're shooting yourself in the foot if you're killing the newsrooms that do it properly."

In September, six journalists with the independent fact-checking platform, Matsda2sh - constituting its entire newsroom - were arrested in home raids by the Egyptian authorities and held incommunicado for nearly a week.

Six journalists working for the independent fact-checking platform Matsda2sh are facing terrorism charges

They have since been charged with joining the Muslim Brotherhood and financing terrorism, and their lawyers report that several were beaten and electrocuted in detention. They say that no evidence has been presented linking them to the Brotherhood.

Egypt's former president Mohammed Morsi – who was backed by the Muslim Brotherhood – was removed from power by the military, led by Abdul Fattah al-Sisi, in July 2013 after widespread protests. Under Sisi, who became president the following year, the Islamist movement was classed as a terrorist organisation, leading to a widespread clampdown.

On Tuesday, a spokesperson for the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Thameen Al-Kheetan, called for the Matsda2sh reporters to be released, with all charges dropped.

He also said the case against Attalah "raises fresh concerns regarding due process and fair trial".

"We call on Egypt to end all forms of harassment of journalists and media outlets, and to respect and fulfil the right to freedom of expression, including the right to information," Al-Kheetan said.

"The steps taken to suppress the continued work of both Matsda2sh and Mada Masr must be overturned. The people of Egypt have a right to read and hear views expressed through these fora on issues of legitimate public concern."

Attalah has suggested the authorities might again be trying to silence independent voices at a time of economic strain in Egypt and regional instability.

It has been widely noted that recent legal action against journalists comes after the US State Department waived human rights conditions on $320m (£240m) in its foreign military funding for Egypt in September. This allowed the funds to be released as part of Washington's annual $1.3bn military aid package.

The BBC asked US Secretary of State Marco Rubio whether he had raised the recent crackdown on independent journalism with Egypt's Foreign Minister, Badr Abdelatty, at their meeting about regional tensions in Paris on Monday.

"We didn't discuss it today," Rubio said. "But… like anything else in foreign policy, there's always a balancing act to further the national interest of the United States. And in the end, Egypt has been a reliable and good defence partner of the United States."

"That doesn't mean you agree with everything another government does," he went on, adding that he was not "opining about their journalists".

Between 10,000 and 13,000 grizzly bears are estimated to live in British Columbia (file image)

Four grizzly bears have been killed in connection with a fatal attack on a mother and daughter in the Canadian province of British Columbia.

Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20, died earlier this month after going on an afternoon walk in a trail area in Bella Coola.

The British Columbia Conservation Office Service (BCCOS) launched an investigation into their deaths and forensic testing has since confirmed a sow and her three cubs were responsible for the attack.

All four were destroyed "in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines" to protect the public, BCCOS Inspector Jeff Tyre said in an update on Tuesday.

Mother and daughter die after suspected grizzly bear attack in Canada

"Evidence from the investigation as well as animal DNA was analysed and conclusively linked to a sow and its three offspring," he added.

The attack "likely involved predatory behaviour", which Tyre said was "very rare".

He added that more than a dozen conservation officers took part in the investigation over the past week, amid "difficult terrain and weather".

Balcarras and Reed were "two peas in a pod" who "got along really, really well" and shared many hobbies, Balcarras' brother, Josh, told CBC.

"When Jenny hiked, Selah was right there beside her," he said.

Tyre said DNA testing also confirmed the four bears were not involved in a 2025 attack on a school group also in the Bella Coola area.

The incident in November of last year saw 11 people injured, two of them critically, while the bear responsible was never found.

"Today, we have learned from the BC Conservation Officer Service members that they have captured and euthanized the bears involved in the recent fatal attack," said Samuel Schooner, Elected Chief of the Nuxalk Nation, in a statement.

"We would like to thank the BC Conservation Officer Service for their dedication and hard work to resolve this incident. This attack has been deeply re-triggering for our community members as we continue to recover from last year's attack. Our thoughts remain with the victims' families."

Mauricio Pochettino has been in charge of the USA since September 2024

After the expected formalities of Michael Carrick's dismissal as Manchester United head coach were completed after a summit meeting in Monaco, Mauricio Pochettino's decade-long courtship with Old Trafford became a full-blown relationship.

Pochettino and United go back a long way, with the Argentine's name associated with the club since he was spotted leaving a lunch appointment at Scott's restaurant in Mayfair with Sir Alex Ferguson in 2016.

Ferguson was three years into his retirement, while Pochettino was building his reputation at Tottenham , where he fashioned an intense, all-out-attacking team that the great Scot admired.

Pochettino called it "a meeting in London between colleagues, between a genius and an apprentice".

Pochettino was mentioned as a contender to succeed Louis van Gaal when he was sacked by United in May 2016, then when Jose Mourinho suffered the same fate in December 2018.

Pochettino was the other name on United's shortlist when Erik ten Hag was appointed in April 2022, then again when the Dutchman was shown the door in October 2024.

Finally he has inherited the Old Trafford empire.

The problem for Pochettino is that the once great footballing empire is crumbling before the eyes, the dysfunctional product of years of poor decision-making and questionable appointments, allied to a Frankenstein's monster of a squad assembled by six managers.

One of Pochettino's quirks is to have a box of lemons in his office, believing they absorb negative energy. He will need several truckloads of the industrial strength variety to suck away the current mood at Old Trafford.

He first had to wait for the official confirmation of Carrick's departure - a long drawn-out affair which dod little credit to part-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Carrick, 45, has proved to be out of his depth since being confirmed as permanent head coach following a successful interim spell, but his history of success as a player, his basic decency and his obvious desire to turn United's fortunes around made the ham-fisted handling of his sacking another uncomfortable episode.

It was an emotion reflected by United's increasingly disaffected fanbase, who have made it clear who they blame for their current place in the Premier League relegation zone.

Pochettino ready to accept Man Utd offer to replace Carrick

The Monaco summit that will decide the future of Carrick and Man Utd

Would Pochettino be the right appointment to replace Carrick? Have your say

Pochettino's appointment lands in the middle ground between the flawed sentimentalism of turning to fan favourites with little or no track record of success, such as Carrick and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, as well as the quick fix of bringing in proven past winners such as Van Gaal and Mourinho.

With his one-time dream of returning to Spurs now seemingly out of reach forever, Pochettino is ready to pick up the reins at the fallen giants that are United, another club he has clearly always had in his sights.

For two more matches he will coach the USA, whom he led at this summer's World Cup. Even then United were lurking on his agenda.

During the campaign Pochettino held court with invited journalists at the USA team hotel in California.

When mention was made of United, Pochettino turned to his closest confidante and ever-present assistant coach Jesus Perez to say: "One day, your dream comes true. You go to Manchester United ."

Perez replied with "United should have got you", promoting the response from a smiling Pochettino: "Future. Future."

The big question now is what Pochettino will United be getting?

He remains a beloved figure at Spurs , where he had an outstanding record of consistency following his appointment from Southampton in May 2014.

He never finished lower than fifth - in his first season - in any full campaign in charge, including second place behind Chelsea in 2016-17 and third in 2015-16 and 2017-18.

The one question mark always placed against Pochettino, including when he finished sixth at Chelsea in 2023-24, was an inability to get his teams over the line to tangible success in England.

Pochettino claimed the first trophies of his managerial career with Paris St-Germain after leaving Spurs - the 2021 French Cup and 2022 Ligue 1 title - but the club's hierarchy felt that was the minimum he should achieve given the squad at his disposal, and he did not see out his contract.

In England with Spurs , he was runner-up in the League Cup in 2014-15 and reached the FA Cup semi-finals in 2016-17 and 2017-18. In 2018-19 he reached the Champions League final and the League Cup semis.

In one season at Chelsea - a loveless relationship in which he could never shed his Spurs connections in the eyes of fans - he reached the FA Cup semi-finals and lost the League Cup final.

Pochettino's driven, competitive nature means that is an itch he will want to scratch.

While Spurs have always appeared to be his first love, there is also no doubt United occupies a special place in his thoughts.

Spanish football expert Guillem Balague, who worked with Pochettino on his book Brave New World, says: "There is a fit with the people at the club too.

"Omar Berrada is a fan. When Manchester City drew up a shortlist to replace Pep Guardiola, some City supporters, including Omar, argued for Pochettino to be on it.

"There are plenty of clues about his feelings for United in the book. He was at the stadium in 1999 when United won the Champions League.

"Sir Alex Ferguson is mentioned 28 times, more than any other name in the biography.

" Spurs tried to push back and cut those references. Pochettino and I talked it over and decided that none of it would be touched. That shows how much it mattered to him."

Pochettino is a renowned builder, as he proved at Spurs after succeeding the sacked Tim Sherwood, working with Harry Kane to develop the recently crowned Ballon d'Or winner, as well as bringing Son Heung-Min to the club for a bargain £22m from Bayer Leverkusen in 2015.

If Pochettino can repeat that - a tough job in United's circumstances - and reproduce the easy-on-the-eye, attacking football played with relentless energy, then he could finally be the perfect fit Ratcliffe has so far looked in vain to discover.

Pochettino is also his own man, so it will be intriguing to see how he works with Ratcliffe, Berrada and Wilcox.

The road to Pochettino's sacking at Spurs effectively started following a friendly win against Real Madrid only weeks after their Champions League final defeat, when he made it clear he was not having enough influence at the club.

He enjoys warm relationships with his players, with a track record of improvement. It was no co-incidence that Cole Palmer enjoyed his best season working under Pochettino at Chelsea , scoring 25 goals in 45 appearances.

Pochettino, however, is also single-minded and ruthless, as he proved with an emphatic response to criticism for not phoning the players he left out of the USA World Cup squad.

He said: "When I was a player, when I didn't make the roster I didn't want my coach to call me. The players who didn't make the roster, they don't want to hear me say 'I apologise'. What are you going to say? Am I going to lie?"

He will need to call on every one of those qualities if and when he assumes control at United.

The final word on that day went to Pochettino as the pair argued over who was picking up the tab.

Ferguson said Pochettino could pay if he named an Argentina player who scored in the 1930 World Cup final.

Pochettino, in what he claimed was a moment of inspiration, named Guillermo Stabile.

He won that argument. Now both he and Ferguson will hope Pochettino can produce more moments of inspiration to win something more substantial at United.

Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October 2026

Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient - the seventh to recover from the virus - marking a major milestone in efforts to contain the disease in the East African nation, which now begins a 42-day countdown to officially being declared Ebola-free.

It had confirmed its first ever case of Ebola early in October when a Kenyan businessman died within days of arriving in the capital, Nairobi.

He had contracted the virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where more than 5,000 people have died in an ongoing outbreak that began in May. His mother also subsequently died.

Kenya's health minister said 135 identified contacts of the infected patients had also completed their 21 days in isolation.

"Today with the discharge of the last patient we can confirm and tell the world that seven patients have recovered - and all contacts have completed their follow-up monitoring," Aden Duale said.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) described it as an important achievement in the regional response to the outbreak.

"This is an encouraging moment for Kenya and for Africa. We must sustain surveillance and vigilance until the outbreak is officially declared over," Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya posted on X.

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

Kenya has reported no new confirmed cases since 20 October.

All the Kenyan cases were linked to the man who had travelled from DR Congo through Uganda, with health officials reporting no evidence of wider community transmission.

Those who have recovered following treatment included four healthcare workers.

Five patients were discharged on 3 November, followed by a sixth three days later, before the final patient was cleared on Wednesday.

Under World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines, 42 days must pass after the last patient tests negative and is discharged, or the last Ebola victim is safely buried, before an outbreak can be declared over.

The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks.

Duale said the government would maintain heightened surveillance at border crossings, airports, health facilities and communities throughout the countdown.

Emergency response teams will remain on alert across the country, while the health authorities will continue monitoring travellers arriving from affected countries.

Kenyans returning from Ebola-affected areas are required to complete electronic health declarations before travelling, undergo screening on arrival and spend 21 days in quarantine under the supervision of health teams.

The minister also urged countries that had imposed travel and visa restrictions to reconsider them - adding that Kenya had no intention of serving as a quarantine centre for another country.

In May, a Kenyan court suspended US plans to open an Ebola quarantine facility for American citizens.

Kenya has maintained that there is no need to restrict domestic travel, trade or public gatherings.

The outbreak has nevertheless disrupted international travel, with some Gulf countries introducing restrictions affecting travellers from Kenya and other African countries.

Saudi Arabia stopped issuing visas to Kenyan nationals in late October, prompting concerns among those seeking employment there.

Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced that it is lifting its suspension on issuing new visas to Ugandan nationals, easing restrictions introduced in June.

But Ugandans will have to spend at least 21 days outside of Uganda before being allowed to travel to the UAE.

The UAE is also allowing certain students, diplomatic passport holders and Ugandan embassy employees to enter under approved health procedures.

Uganda, which shares a long and busy border with DR Congo, was among the countries first affected but declared its own Ebola outbreak over on 27 August.

The current outbreak in DR Congo has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

Danny Kelly worked for the BBC until 2007

Former BBC radio presenter Danny Kelly has been described as a "broadcasting titan" following his death at the age of 69.

Kelly stepped back from his long-term role at Talksport after being diagnosed with throat cancer in March.

He presented a radio sports show on BBC London before joining Talksport in 2007 and was previously editor of the New Musical Express and Q magazine.

Talksport paid tribute to him on Wednesday, calling him a "much-loved friend" and a "broadcasting titan".

"A true legend of the station, Danny had time for everyone and went out of his way to be kind," they said. , external

"His genuine warmth and incredible passion for broadcasting will be sorely missed by all of us."

They added: "A cherished part of Talksport for so many years, Danny brought extraordinary wit, warmth and knowledge to our airwaves.

"His passion for football, music and life was infectious, and his kindness touched everyone around him."

Kelly also presented BBC radio shows in the 1990s with Danny Baker, who described him as a "great friend, supreme broadcaster and funniest man I ever knew".

Kelly was a lifelong Tottenham fan and the Premier League club said he was "one of our own".

A club statement , external added: "Our thoughts and love are with his family and friends at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Danny."

BBC Radio 5 Live's George Cummins was a friend and former colleague of Kelly at Talksport.

"Danny had an extraordinary knowledge of music and football," he said. "His ability to combine the two on air made him an incredible broadcaster.

"His brilliant wit made him an amazing story teller. Colleagues would often remark that his brain was like an encyclopaedia.

"While he was a genius on-air, it was his personality off-air that would shine through. He was always there to give advice and help. He always took an interest in colleagues' lives away from work.

"He was a very positive man. He loved his job. He loved entertaining the nation. I'll always remember a great friend who taught me so much."

Consultant doctors in England have called off their two-day strike this month to hold talks with the government.

The walkout was due begin on 25 November at 06:59 GMT, with consultants staffing emergency care only.

This is known as Christmas Day cover and was likely to have a major impact on most routine and elective or planned services.

But the British Medical Association, the trade union for doctors, said it was pausing the action to discuss pay and working conditions with the government.

Consultants – the most senior doctors in hospitals – were given a 3.5% pay increase this year.

But the BMA argues pay has fallen by a quarter over the past 17 years, once inflation is taken into account – although this is using a measure of inflation that tends to be higher than the one favoured by economists.

The union also wants a reduction in the standard working week, from 40 to 35 hours, and higher pay for out-of-hours work, alongside changes to pensions, including greater flexibility over when they can be taken.

Meetings have been taking place over recent months, but the BMA is now entering formal talks with the government's negotiating team. They could start as soon as this week.

In a statement, BMA consultants committee co-chairs Dr Helen Neary and Dr Shanu Datta said: "We welcome the opportunity to enter formal negotiations with the government and hope this marks a turning point in a dispute that has gone on for far too long.

"We've always said strikes do not need to go ahead as long as the government is willing to genuinely negotiate and now is their chance to do so.

"We have received assurances that there are no constraints on what we discuss in these negotiations, and we look forward to hearing their proposals on both pay and working conditions."

But government sources said giving them a bigger pay rise this year was not on the table because of the state of the public finances and current level of their pay.

Average earnings for consultants top £150,000 a year.

Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said the cancellation of the strike was "welcome news for patients and the wider NHS".

"I had a constructive discussion with the BMA on reforms that could give consultants a stronger voice, greater flexibility and more freedom to innovate, while improving services for patients."

In the strike ballot, 76% of consultants who took part voted in favour of strike action, with just over half of eligible BMA members taking part.

The government says this represents only around one in five consultants employed by the NHS in England voting for strike action, as nearly half are not BMA members.

These children had to leave their primary school in Rome as a result of one of the threats sent on Wednesday

Some 6,300 schools across Italy and more than 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats, according to local authorities.

In Italy a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution but Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger".

"These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook.

Scotland's education secretary Mairi McAllan said there was no risk to the public and specialist cyber-crime officers were working to identify the source of the messages. In Northern Ireland education officials told schools to remain open unless otherwise advised by police.

It is unclear whether the incidents are connected.

"As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," McAllan said.

Scottish police had earlier said that the warnings were "immediately assessed" as hoaxes. However some local authorities confirmed that some schools had been evacuated.

"Our advice is that there is no requirement to evacuate schools or keep children away from education based solely on the content of the emails," Police Scotland said.

Italian officials said a single email appeared to have been sent on Wednesday to the inboxes of 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 state schools, and private schools were unaffected.

The message, said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan", caused alarm in many schools.

The BBC has seen the email sent to Scottish schools which appeared to have similar wording, and also referenced the name Mikhail Andropov, although as leader of a "Red Owl" project.

Italy's Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said the incidents involving Italian schools were probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk", adding that there appeared to be a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in across Europe targeting flights, supermarkets and even hospitals.

Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption.

Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings.

No risk to public from hoax school bomb threats, says government minister

Police treating threatening email sent to more than 300 schools as 'hoax'

On Wednesday one Milan headteacher, Anna Bertato, told Italian media she had checked the email address of the sender online: "It was already classified as spam by a student at a university in Taiwan."

Another Milan headteacher, Massimo Nunzio Barrella, told Adnkronos news agency that he had immediately realised the email was spam when it arrived in his inbox at 08:59 and he decided not to evacuate his school and reassured parents who phoned in.

"The text seemed almost comical," said Barrella, "it was like a message from Martians: 'We have come to annihilate you.' I even had a bit of a laugh."

Although many schools were initially evacuated on Wednesday, the alarm was quickly lifted, and pupils were allowed to return to class. Some parents decided to take their children home for the day, but the majority of schools in Milan did not send their pupils home.

Some 280 school head teachers had already received threats in recent days, according to Italian reports.

In a statement, the head of the central Umbria region Stefania Proietti said "checks conducted so far in Umbrian schools have proved negative, and law enforcement is working rapidly and carefully to verify each report".

Abantu 11,000 ni bo bamaze kwemezwa ko banduye Ebola mu cyorezo cyadutse ku nshuro ya 17 muri Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (RDC), nkuko bikubiye mu mibare mishya yatangajwe n'abategetsi bo mu rwego rw'ubuvuzi muri icyo gihugu.

Raporo ikubiyemo iyo mibare ivuga ko ubu abantu 11,042 bamaze kwemezwa ko banduye Ebola, mu gihe abantu 5,387 bemejwe ko bishwe na yo kuva itangajwe ku itariki ya 15 Gicurasi (5) uyu mwaka.

Muri iyo raporo nshya yo kugeza ku itariki ya 9 Ugushyingo (11) uyu mwaka, abategetsi bemeje ko abantu bashya 52 banduye Ebola naho abandi bantu bashya 33 irabica.

Abo bantu bashya banduye Ebola bagaragaye mu ntara za Ituri, Kivu ya Ruguru na Haut-Uélé.

Abategetsi bo mu rwego rw'ubuvuzi bavuga ko intara ya Ituri ikiri izingiro ry'iki cyorezo, ikaba yihariye hafi 70% by'abantu bose bamaze kwemezwa ko banduye ku rwego rw'igihugu.

Intara ya Kivu ya Ruguru ni yo iza ku mwanya wa kabiri mu kwibasirwa cyane n'iki cyorezo ndetse ikomeje kugira igipimo cy'abicwa na Ebola kiruta igipimo rusange cyo ku rwego rw'igihugu.

Iyi mibare mishya inagaragaza ingorane zikomeje kubaho mu guhangana n'iki cyorezo. 79.7% by'abantu bamenyekanye ko bahuye n'abanduye ni bo bonyine bashoboye gukurikiranwa neza kugeza icyo gihe iyo mibare yatangarijwe.

Icyo gipimo kiri munsi y'intego ya 95% – yo gukurikirana neza abagize aho bahurira n'abanduye – ifatwa ko ari ngombwa kugira ngo uruhererekane rw'ubwandu rushobore guhagarikwa.

Abategetsi banatangaje ko umutekano mucye wabangamiye ibikorwa byo guhangana na Ebola, ugatinza ibikorwa byo guhemba bamwe mu bakozi bakorera aho iki cyorezo cyiganje ndetse ahantu henshi hakaba harabayeho ibikorwa byo kurwanya ingamba zo gupima Ebola.

Abategetsi bo mu rwego rw'ubuvuzi bavuga ko amakuru atari ukuri ayobya akomeje gukwirakwira hamwe na hamwe mu baturage, ibyo bigatuma ibikorwa byo kumenya abanduye bigorana ndetse ibyo bikanabangamira ibikorwa byo gushishikariza abantu kujya kwivuza hakiri kare.

Nubwo hari izo ngorane, nta karere k'ubuzima gashya katangaje umurwayi wa mbere wa Ebola muri iki gihe cy'itangazwa ry'imibare mishya. Abarwayi 39 basezerewe mu bitaro nyuma yuko bakize, bituma umubare wose hamwe w'abamaze gukira Ebola uba abantu 2,990. Ibikorwa byo gukingira no kugenzura Ebola birakomeje mu ntara irangwamo.

Antoine Dupont's experience starting at fly-half is limited to a handful of games for Toulouse

France captain Antoine Dupont will fill in at fly-half for Friday's Nations Championship game against world champions South Africa in Paris.

Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, who was born and raised in London but moved to France as a 19-year-old after struggling to get a professional contract in England, will win his fourth cap on the wing.

Grandidier-Nkanang focused on Sevens, winning Olympic gold alongside Dupont in 2024 before making a successful switch back to the 15-a-side game with Pau.

Dupont, a specialist scrum-half with only a handful of appearances at 10, has been forced into fly-half by the absence of Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack, Thomas Ramos and Antoine Hastoy.

It had been expected that Maxime Lucu, another scrum-half, would play at fly-half.

Lucu came off the bench to replace Ntamack, who suffered a shoulder injury 32 minutes into Saturday's 54-17 victory over Fiji.

Lucu has the more recent experience as a starting fly-half at club level, having played at 10 for Bordeaux-Begles against Gloucester last month.

However, France coach Fabian Galthie has opted for Dupont, who filled in at fly-half for Toulouse during an injury crisis in the 2023-24 season.

Galthie has selected hooker Julien Marchand and number eight Gregory Alldritt, who was left out of this year's Six Nations, to counter the Springboks' forward power.

"I don't even know if Dupont's team-mates know exactly what he's going to do next, so he's just really playing on instinct, which is tough to handle," South Africa coach Erasmus said this week.

He has made only one change to the side that thrashed Italy 66-7 on Saturday, with Wilco Louw replacing former Bath prop Thomas du Toit.

South Africa have won nine of their past 10 Tests against France, including a 14-man victory last autumn and a one-point quarter-final victory at the 2023 World Cup.

England are closing in on reaching the knockout rounds of the 2026-27 Uefa Nations League

England go into their final two 2026-27 Nations League matches on the brink of qualification for the quarter-finals.

Thomas Tuchel's side sit second after four matches in Group A3, with a point in either of their final two matches in November against Croatia and Spain enough to secure a place in the final eight teams.

November's international break is the final two full rounds of matches, with four rounds already complete.

The eight teams to finish in the top two of the four League A groups will play in the knockout rounds that start in March 2027.

Teams finishing at the top of groups in leagues B and C will earn promotion for the next Nations League cycle, while teams that finish second in a League B or League C group will face either a third-placed or bottom-placed team from the league above them in a promotion/relegation play-off.

The two worst sides to finish bottom of a League A group are automatically relegated. The other bottom sides in League A, third-placed sides in League A and bottom-placed sides in League B are at risk of relegation.

The losers of the play-offs will be relegated.

As the Nations League format is changing for the next cycle, taking place across 2028 and 2029, all League D teams are guaranteed promotion to League C.

Additionally, no teams from League C will be relegated at the end of this cycle.

The new format will consist of three larger leagues, meaning there will not be a League D in the next campaign.

Portugal and Spain are the only sides guaranteed to play in the quarter-finals at present, having both won their opening four matches.

England, who are three points behind Spain in Group A3, are six points clear of third-placed Croatia and with a significantly superior head-to-head record. Unless England were to lose 7-0 or worse to Croatia on Thursday, the Three Lions will be certain of a place in the last eight.

In Group A1, France and Italy sit in the top two spots. Belgium are a point behind Italy in third. Two of those three sides will advance to the quarter-finals.

It is a similar tale in Group A2. Netherlands and Greece are the top two, three points clear of Germany in third. With Serbia bottom on zero points, two of the current top three will advance.

In A4, Denmark are second and three points clear of Wales and Norway. One of the trio will join table-toppers Portugal.

The quarter-finals are played across two legs in March's international break.

The winners of each tie will advance to the semi-finals in June 2027, which are played in a one-off match across Wednesday 9 and Thursday 10 June. The final takes place on Sunday, 13 June.

Wales are in a three-way battle alongside Norway and Denmark to qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals

While England's League A campaign has gone well so far, Wales' has been trickier.

In a tough group with Portugal, Denmark and Norway, Wales have picked up three points from four games after beating Norway 2-1 in Cardiff.

With Portugal already qualified for the last eight, Wales will need close to maximum points in their final matches against Norway and Portugal to stand any chance of making the last eight.

A third-place finish would put them in a play-off to avoid relegation in March, while coming last in the group may ensure a drop down to League B.

Scotland are now unable to reach the top spot in Group B1 and are unlikely to make the promotion/relegation play-offs.

In order to finish second, Scotland need to win both of their final two games and hope Slovenia pick up no more than a point from theirs. Alternatively, Scotland can pick up four points and finish second, providing Slovenia lose their final two matches.

Northern Ireland have had a successful international break with two wins, two draws and no goals conceded in their four matches in Group B2.

They sit top of the group by a point, with their remaining matches against bottom side Ukraine and second-place Hungary.

Should they beat Ukraine and Hungary fail to beat Georgia in November's first round of fixtures, they will guarantee top spot and promotion. A win for them and Hungary doing the same would mean the two sides face off in a promotion-decider in the final round of games.

The Republic of Ireland are third in Group B3 following five points from their first four matches.

Their remaining two fixtures are against the top two teams Austria and Kosovo. Wins in both would guarantee a top-two finish and would also put them in a strong position to win the group, depending on goal difference and the result of Austria's meeting with Israel.

Spain are the current holders of the European Championship, beating England in the 2024 final

Once the Nations League campaign is concluded, all 54 competing nations will be ranked based on their performance in this edition of the competition.

That ranking will have a direct impact on qualification for the 2028 European Championships, being held in England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

The Nations League ranking will also determine the seeding of nations for Euro 2028 qualification.

Regular qualifying will take place between March and November 2027, with play-offs for the remaining spots in the tournament to take place in March 2028.

As there are four co-hosts and none of them have been granted immediate qualification, the number of how many qualify will effectively determine how many play-off spots will be up for grabs.

Uefa have said that up to two places will be given to the best-ranked co-hosts that fail to qualify for the tournament via its primary qualification route.

Scenarios have already been designed for occurrences where either two, one or zero co-hosts are given entry spots.

Depending on which play-off format is required, either eight or 12 teams will enter.

A total of 24 teams will enter the European Championships, 20 of them will consist of the winners of the 12 qualifying groups and the eight best runners-up from those group.

The remaining runners-up will enter the play-offs, alongside the Nations League group winners from League A, League B and League C that failed to finish in the top two of their Euro 2028 qualifying group.

If extra teams are required, the best-ranked League D group winner will enter the play-offs.

Any additional play-off spots that become available after that will filter down to the next-highest ranked Nations League finishers until the play-off spots are filled.

Reta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika zagabishije Madagascar ku bijanye no gukomeza ubucuti ifitaniye n'Uburusiya, zivuga ko ugukorana nk'ukwo intwaro z'abasirikare zagiranye n'Uburusiya mu bihugu vyo muri Afrika y'Uburengero kutashoboye gutuma umutekano utera imbere.

Icegera c'umuyobozi ajejwe ibikorwa vy'igisirikare ca Amerika muri Afrika, Lt Gen John Brennan, yavuze ko kuba Madagascar iherereye mu karere k'ibahari Indiyano bituma igira uruhara rukomeye mu bijanye n'urudandaza mpuzamakungu.

Yagabishije ico gihugu kudakurikiza "uburorero bwo muri Sahel", avuga ko bushobora gutuma umutekano muke urushiriza gukwira ku mugabane wa Afrika.

Ibihugu vya Mali, Burkina Faso na Niger, vyose birongowe n'abasirikare, vyarahagaritse ubucuti bwavyo n'ibihugu vyo mu Burengero, bihitamwo kwitura Uburusiya kugira ngo bubifashe mu vya gisirikare mu rugamba birimwo rwo kurwanya imihari y'abajihadiste.

Uburusiya bwaraguye imigenderanire mu vya gisirikare na Madagascar kuva abasirikare bafashe ubutegetsi muri ico gihugu mu 2025. Buyirungikira ibirwanisho hamwe n'abamenyereza mu vya gisirikare.

Mu kiganiro n'abamenyeshamakuru biciye kuri internet, Brennan yagize ati: "Turatewe umutima uhagaze n'ukuntu Uburusiya bushaka gukwiragiza akarorero ko muri Sahel mu bindi bice vy'umugabane wa Afrika".

Yabandanije ati: « Madagascar iherereye ahantu hahambaye cane, co kimwe na Mozambike, rero ntitwipfuza kubona ubwo burorero bukoreshwa muri ivyo bihugu bibiri".

Abategetsi b'ibihugu bitatu vyo mu karere ka Sahel bari babanje kwagiriza ibihugu vyo mu burengero vyahoze ari ibifatanyabikorwa ko bitashoboye guhagarika imihari y'abajihadiste, imbere y'uko bahindukirira Moscou kugira ngo ibifashe.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Ariko rero, ibitero vy'iyo mihari vyarabandanije, n'ubwo ivyo bihugu vyongereje ugufashanya n'Uburusiya mu vya gisirikare.

Brennan yagaragaje kandi impungenge zijanye n'umutekano mu muhora wo mu kiyaga ca Mozambike (Mozambique Channel), utandukanya Mozambike na Madagasikari n'umugabane wa Afrika. Uwo muhora ni inzira ihambaye ikoreshwa mu gutwara ibidandazwa hagati y'ibihugu.

Yavuze ko ari ngirakamaro cane gukingira ibikorwa vyo mu mazi, kugira ngo abarwanyi bafitaniye isano n'umuhari wiyita 'reta ya kiislam' mu buraruko bwa Mozambike hamwe n'abandi bashobora guhungabanya umutekano ntibabibangamire.

Afatiye ku biheruka kuba ku nkengera z'ico gihugu bifitaniye isano n'ubusuma bwo mu kiyaga, Brennan yavuze ko imihari y'abarwanyi mu buraruko bwa Mozambike iriko irahindura imikenyuro ikoresha mu bikorwa vy'ubugizi bwa nabi vyayo, harimwo no kurushiriza guteza imbere ubushobozi bwo kugaba ibitero biciye mu mazi.

Yavuze ko abafatanyabikorwa ba Amerika "bafise umwidegemvyo wo gukorana n'abo bashaka", ariko abahimiriza gutahura ingaruka bishobora kugira.

Madagasikari ntaco irashikiriza ku mugaragaro ku majambo ya Brennan.

Perezida Michaël Randrianirina aherutse gusubira gushimangira ko ashigikiye ko ubucuti hagati y'Uburusiya n'ibihugu vya Afrika burushiriza gukomera.

Mu nama y'Uburusiya na Afrika yabaye mu kwezi guheze, Madagasikari n'Uburusiya vyarashize umukono ku masezerano atari make y'ugufashanya mu bijanye n'ukwivuna abansi, ingenzi n'urudandazwa.

Muri Ruhuhuma (2), inyuma y'amezi makeyi afashe ubutegetsi biciye mu guhirika ubutegetsi, Randrianirina yaciye agendera Moscou. Wari umusi wa mbere mu myaka hafi 50 umukuru w'igihugu ca Madagasikari agendeye icese Uburusiya.
